findings.detail: The `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2_100))` exists to push the two builds past the ZIP's 2-second time resolution so a wall-clock-stamped entry shows up as a byte difference. But the assertion added three lines later — `Object.values(zip.files).map(f => [f.name, f.date.getTime()])` equals every entry paired with `EXTRACTED_AT.getTime()` — already catches exactly that bug deterministically and instantly: an implicitly-created `source/` folder carries `new Date()`, which fails the date assertion regardless of how fast the two builds run. So the sleep buys no additional coverage of the regression this PR fixes, while adding 2.1 s of pure wall clock to every `npm test` run and to every CI job. It does still guard a broader class (any other wall-clock-derived nondeterminism in `generateAsync`), which is why this is `low` rather than a request — if you want to keep that broader guard, keeping the sleep is a defensible trade, but it should be a conscious one.
findings.summary: The 2.1 s sleep is redundant with the per-entry date assertion below it

findings.detail: `f.date.getTime()` is read back from the ZIP's DOS timestamp, which stores seconds in 2-second steps and has no millisecond field. The assertion is exact, so it only passes because `EXTRACTED_AT` (line 32) happens to be `2026-09-29T18:15:08.000Z` — even second, zero milliseconds. `EXTRACTED_AT` is shared by six other tests in this file; anyone changing it to an odd second or a non-zero millisecond to serve one of those will break this assertion with a confusing off-by-one-second diff that points at `buildBundle` rather than at the constant. Not a defect in this PR — recording it so the coupling is visible.
findings.summary: New assertion silently depends on EXTRACTED_AT having an even, ms-zero second
